mechanism: PARG reverses PARylation, so blocking it traps poly(ADP-ribose) on chromatin during replication. In cells already running hot on replication stress, that tips stalled forks into collapse and leaves single-stranded DNA gaps behind Okazaki fragments, which kills the cell. The dependency is strongest where fork-protection genes such as TIMELESS, TIPIN and CLASPIN are low.
rationale: This tumor is genomically unstable and BRCA-proficient, the high-replication-stress HGSOC background where PARG inhibition has been most active in cell lines and xenografts. It acts through a different lesion than PARP trapping, so it is a candidate where a genomic-instability rationale holds even though a BRCA-mutation gate does not. Sensitivity tracks with markers (ssDNA gaps, low fork-protection gene expression) that could be checked on this patient's tumor first.
novelty: Tool-compound PARG inhibition (PDD00017273) has no registered trial; the clinical-grade molecule IDE161 is a separate program and is not in this patient's indication.

key_manuscripts.finding: Across a panel of ovarian cancer lines, PARG inhibition selectively killed cells carrying an underlying DNA-replication vulnerability while sparing normal fallopian-tube and stromal cells.
PARG-inhibitor sensitivity across ovarian preclinical models correlated with accumulation of single-stranded DNA gaps, pointing to a usable response biomarker.

developability: PDD00017273 is a laboratory probe, not a clinical molecule. A clinical-grade PARG inhibitor such as IDE161 would be the realistic vehicle, and a response-biomarker assay would need to be in hand first.
risks: No validated patient-selection assay for PARG dependence yet
Replication-stress agents can carry bone-marrow toxicity, which matters against this patient's myelosuppression veto
Most data are cell-line based; depth and durability of in vivo responses are limited
caveats: Sensitivity is confined to a replication-stressed subset, so the qualitative genomic-instability call here is suggestive rather than confirmatory.

mechanism: RAD51 drives the strand-invasion step of homologous recombination. Probes such as B02 and the more potent B02 isomer block RAD51 filament formation, which suppresses HR and pushes cells toward error-prone repair. The idea is to force an HR-deficient state pharmacologically and pair it with a DNA-damaging or PARP-trapping agent.
rationale: A genomically unstable but BRCA-proficient HGSOC still has functional RAD51, so chemically dialing down HR is one route to mimic the deficiency PARP inhibitors exploit. In cell models, B02-class compounds reduce HR and sensitize to olaparib. The appeal here is a non-genetic path to PARP sensitization in a BRCA-wild-type tumor.
novelty: B02 and its isomer are academic chemical probes with no IND; the one clinical RAD51-pathway agent, CYT-0851, was later reclassified as acting mainly through MCT1, so a genuine clinical RAD51 inhibitor does not exist yet.

key_manuscripts.finding: Identified B02 as a specific small-molecule inhibitor of human RAD51 from a high-throughput screen.
Described B02-isomer derivatives that inhibit homologous recombination more potently than B02 and sensitize triple-negative breast cancer cells to olaparib.

developability: These are bench reagents with modest potency and no clinical-grade successor. A drug-like RAD51 inhibitor would have to be developed before the idea could reach a patient.
risks: Systemic HR suppression could be genotoxic to normal tissue
Potency and selectivity of current probes are weak
The CYT-0851 story shows how easily a RAD51-inhibitor phenotype can come from an off-target mechanism

intervention_label: cGAS-STING agonism exploiting chromosomal instability, paired with the IL-12 axis
mechanism: Chromosomally unstable tumors spill DNA into the cytosol through micronuclei, which the cGAS-STING sensor reads as danger and turns into type-I interferon and T-cell recruitment. A STING agonist would push on that same axis deliberately. Layered onto the patient's on-study IL-12 plasmid, the two could feed the innate-to-adaptive handoff from different angles.
rationale: The tumor's genomic instability is the substrate cGAS-STING responds to, and the patient is already on an IL-12 immunogene therapy, so an agonist that warms the microenvironment could be complementary rather than redundant. That matters in an MSS, low-TMB tumor unlikely to respond to single-agent checkpoint blockade. The combination is a hypothesis, not a tested regimen.
novelty: No program pairs a STING agonist with IL-12 immunogene therapy in HGSOC; STING agonists exist in other settings, but this case-specific combination and rationale are undeveloped.

key_manuscripts.finding: Showed that ongoing chromosomal instability sustains a cytosolic-DNA response through cGAS-STING, linking copy-number instability to innate immune signaling.
Reported MSA-2, an orally available non-nucleotide STING agonist with antitumor activity in mouse models.
In an ovarian tumor model, pairing manganese (a cGAS-STING enhancer) with IL-12 shifted the tumor microenvironment toward a more inflamed, immune-active state.

developability: STING agonists have been hard to deliver and dose safely, and systemic inflammation is a real concern. Pairing one with an active IL-12 therapy would need careful sequencing and dose work in models before any patient test.
risks: Systemic STING activation can drive cytokine toxicity that compounds an already active IL-12 therapy
Chronic STING signaling can turn immunosuppressive or pro-metastatic in some contexts
No data exist for this specific combination
caveats: Treat this as a direction for modeling, not a regimen; the interaction with on-study IL-12 could be antagonistic as easily as additive.

intervention_label: PI3Kalpha targeted-degradation (PROTAC) concept for PIK3CA amplification
mechanism: A PROTAC degrader removes the PI3Kalpha protein rather than just blocking its kinase pocket, which lowers both catalytic and scaffolding output. For an amplified, overexpressed gene, cutting total protein could in principle counter the gene-dosage effect that catalytic inhibitors leave untouched. Reported PI3K degraders achieve potent degradation and show antitumor activity in animal models.
rationale: This tumor carries a focal PIK3CA amplification rather than a hotspot mutation, and the catalytic inhibitors already on the case list (alpelisib, buparlisib) were built for mutant or pathway-active disease. A degrader is a mechanistically distinct option whose protein-lowering action maps more naturally onto an amplification lesion. The link is reasoned, not yet shown for amplification specifically.
novelty: PI3Kalpha degraders are preclinical chemical-biology compounds with no oncology program in HGSOC, and they are a separate modality from the catalytic PI3K inhibitors surfaced upstream.

key_manuscripts.finding: Reported potent PROTAC degraders of PI3K with antitumor activity in vivo, showing that selective PI3K degradation is achievable in animal models.
A commentary making the case for selectively degrading mutant PI3Kalpha as a precision strategy distinct from kinase inhibition.

developability: Current PI3Kalpha degraders are early discovery compounds, and the published work targets mutant or wild-type enzyme rather than the amplification setting here. A clinical-grade degrader and amplification-specific validation would both be needed.
risks: The amplification-to-degrader rationale is unproven; most data concern mutant PI3Kalpha
On-target metabolic toxicity (hyperglycemia) tracks the whole PI3Kalpha axis
No clinical-grade molecule exists

intervention_label: Oral ER PROTAC degrader (vepdegestrant / ARV-471) repurposed for ER-positive ovarian cancer
mechanism: An oral ER PROTAC such as vepdegestrant binds the estrogen receptor and an E3 ligase at once, tagging ER for degradation rather than only blocking ligand binding. That removes receptor protein more completely than an aromatase inhibitor, which only lowers the estrogen supply. The aim in ER-positive disease is deeper, more durable suppression of ER signaling.
rationale: This HGSOC is ER-positive, and the patient prefers low-burden oral therapy, which fits an oral ER degrader. It is a different mechanism from the aromatase inhibition already on the case, so it is a distinct lever on the same ER feature rather than a repeat. PR-negativity tempers the expected magnitude, and all supporting efficacy data are in breast cancer.
novelty: Vepdegestrant is in late-stage breast-cancer development but has no ovarian-cancer program, so its use in ER-positive HGSOC is a repurposing hypothesis rather than an existing clinical option.

key_manuscripts.finding: Vepdegestrant degraded wild-type and mutant ER and was active as monotherapy and with CDK4/6 or PI3K/mTOR inhibitors across ER-positive breast cancer models.

developability: The molecule is clinically mature in breast cancer, so a repurposing trial in ER-positive ovarian cancer is conceivable, but no ovarian preclinical package exists yet to justify one.
risks: No ovarian-specific efficacy data
ER positivity predicts response inconsistently in HGSOC, and PR-negativity here is a further discount
Benefit may be modest relative to the endocrine options already in play
caveats: Distinct from the aromatase-inhibition rationale already on the case; whether fuller ER degradation adds anything in ovarian disease is untested.

intervention_label: MAP2K7 (MKK7) paralog-dependency synthetic-lethal concept for MAP2K4-deleted tumors
mechanism: MAP2K4 (MKK4) and MAP2K7 (MKK7) are paralogous kinases that both feed JNK stress signaling. When one paralog is deleted, cells can lean harder on the other, the setup behind many paralog synthetic-lethal pairs. The concept is that MAP2K4-deleted tumors may become dependent on MAP2K7, making MKK7 a candidate vulnerability.
rationale: This tumor carries a focal somatic MAP2K4 deletion, and paralog dependency is a recurring theme in functional-genomics screens, so MKK7 is a logical place to look for a matched vulnerability. No matched therapy exists for MAP2K4 loss today, which is why a synthetic-lethal angle is worth naming. This is a hypothesis with no direct experimental support in MAP2K4-deleted ovarian cancer.
novelty: A not-yet-drugged conceptual target: no MAP2K7-selective clinical-grade inhibitor and no MAP2K4-loss synthetic-lethal program exist, and it is distinct from the MAP2K4 re-expression idea already logged as preclinical evidence.
developability: There is no MAP2K7-selective inhibitor of clinical quality, and the synthetic-lethal relationship itself would need demonstrating first, ideally in isogenic MAP2K4-deleted models. This sits several validation steps from a patient.
risks: The paralog dependency is assumed, not shown, for MAP2K4 loss
JNK signaling is context-dependent and can be tumor-suppressive, so MKK7 inhibition could backfire
No tool compound with adequate selectivity exists
caveats: Purely conceptual; included as an audit-trail direction for the one feature on this case with no matched therapy.

mechanism: WRN helicase becomes essential in microsatellite-unstable cells, which build up toxic secondary DNA structures at expanded repeats that WRN is needed to resolve. Inhibiting WRN triggers DNA damage and death selectively in MSI tumors, with no effect in microsatellite-stable cells.
rationale: Logged as an audit trail: WRN inhibition is a marquee genomic-instability synthetic-lethal target, but the relevant instability is MSI, not the copy-number instability this BRCA-proficient HGSOC shows.
exclusion_reason: WRN synthetic lethality is MSI-specific and this tumor is microsatellite-stable, so the dependency does not apply (case_match none). The lead compound HRO761 is also already in clinical testing, which would place it with the trial screener.

key_manuscripts.finding: HRO761 selectively impaired MSI cancer cells with no effect in microsatellite-stable cells, and has entered clinical testing for MSI tumors.

mechanism: USP1 deubiquitinates components of the replication and translesion-synthesis machinery, and HR-deficient cells depend on it to tolerate replication stress. KSQ-4279 inhibits USP1, causing fork dysregulation and ssDNA-gap accumulation, and restores sensitivity in PARP-resistant HR-deficient tumors.
rationale: Evaluated as a PARP-resistance and HRD vulnerability with strong ovarian PDX data, but it has moved past the preclinical horizon this scan covers.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage: KSQ-4279 entered a phase 1 solid-tumor trial in 2021, so it belongs to the trial screener rather than this forward-looking scan.

key_manuscripts.finding: KSQ-4279 combined with a PARP inhibitor produced durable regressions across PARP-resistant ovarian and TNBC PDX models.

mechanism: POLtheta runs the backup microhomology-mediated end-joining pathway and is synthetic-lethal with HR deficiency. Novobiocin, an old antibiotic, binds the POLtheta ATPase domain and kills HR-deficient tumors, including PARP-resistant ones, in mouse models.
rationale: A strong genomic-instability synthetic-lethal direction with a clean repurposing story, but it has crossed into clinical testing since first described. Worth noting that the BRCA-wild-type, copy-number-instability setting here is less validated than the BRCA-mutant setting where POLtheta data are strongest.
exclusion_reason: Now clinical-stage: novobiocin is in a phase 1 trial for DNA-repair-deficient and PARP-resistant tumors (NCT05687110), and dedicated POLtheta inhibitors are also in trials, so this axis sits with the trial screener.

key_manuscripts.finding: Identified novobiocin as a POLtheta inhibitor that selectively kills HR-deficient breast and ovarian tumors, including PARP-inhibitor-resistant models.

intervention_label: CDK4/6 inhibitor + aromatase inhibitor (e.g. ribociclib or palbociclib + letrozole)
mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibition blocks cyclin-D-driven Rb phosphorylation and stalls the cell cycle, and adding estrogen deprivation deepens the block in ER-positive disease. The pairing is standard in ER-positive breast cancer.
rationale: An attractive low-toxicity oral pairing on paper for this ER-positive patient, but it has already been tested clinically in ovarian cancer, with most benefit seen in low-grade rather than high-grade serous disease.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage in ovarian cancer: phase 2 trials of ribociclib + letrozole (NCT03673124) and palbociclib + letrozole (LACOG 1018) have run in ER-positive ovarian cancer, so this belongs to the trial screener.

intervention_label: HER2 PROTAC degrader (tucatinib-based tool compound CH7C4)
mechanism: A PROTAC links a HER2-binding warhead, here built on the kinase inhibitor tucatinib, to an E3-ligase recruiter, tagging the HER2 protein for proteasomal destruction rather than only blocking its kinase pocket. Pulling the receptor out cuts both its catalytic signaling and its scaffolding role. The reported compound CH7C4 degrades HER2 with a DC50 of 69 nM and near-complete (96%) maximal degradation.
rationale: This tumor is HER2-low by IHC, and a degrader is the one HER2-directed modality not already on the case as an ADC. The honest problem is that the published proof sits in HER2-amplified breast cells, where HER2 is the oncogenic driver; in a HER2-low tumor the receptor is unlikely to be what the cell depends on, so removing it may do little. I am logging it as a HER2-directed direction to track, not as a worked-out rationale for IHC 1+ disease.
novelty: CH7C4 and related HER2 degraders are discovery-stage chemical-biology compounds with no IND or registered trial, and they are a different modality from the HER2 ADCs the trial and clinical agents already cover.

key_manuscripts.finding: A tucatinib-based PROTAC, CH7C4, degraded HER2 with a DC50 of 69 nM and 96% maximal degradation, and suppressed BT-474 breast cancer growth with about 73% tumor growth inhibition in xenografts. All of the work was in HER2-amplified models.

developability: CH7C4 is a laboratory compound, not a clinical molecule, and no HER2 degrader has reached an oncology trial. Before this could be tested here someone would need a drug-like degrader and, more basically, evidence that a HER2-low tumor depends on HER2 at all.
risks: HER2-low tumors are generally not HER2-driven, so degrading the receptor may have little antitumor effect
All efficacy data are in HER2-amplified breast models, not HER2-low or ovarian disease
No clinical-grade HER2 degrader exists
caveats: Mechanistically this fits HER2-amplified disease far better than the IHC 1+ tumor in front of us.

intervention_label: HER2-TKI priming to raise ADC delivery in HER2-low tumors (TKI + HER2 ADC)
mechanism: HER2 tyrosine-kinase inhibitors change how much receptor sits on the cell surface and how fast it cycles inside. Reversible inhibitors like lapatinib stabilize HER2 and let it pile up at the membrane, while irreversible ones like pyrotinib speed HER2 internalization, and both routes have raised antibody or ADC uptake in models. The idea is to use a TKI to make a low-HER2 tumor briefly more visible or more permeable to a HER2 ADC.
rationale: The hard part of treating a HER2-low (IHC 1+) tumor with a HER2 ADC is that there is little antigen to bind and internalize. Priming with a TKI to nudge surface HER2 up, or to speed payload delivery, is a way to try to widen that narrow window. The catch is that every supporting study used HER2-amplified breast or gastric models, so whether priming lifts an IHC 1+ ovarian tumor enough to matter is untested.
novelty: No clinical program tests TKI priming to turn a HER2-low tumor into a more ADC-targetable state; the TKI-plus-ADC combinations that reached patients were all in HER2-amplified disease, so this is a repurposing hypothesis rather than an existing option.

key_manuscripts.finding: Lapatinib blocked HER2 ubiquitination and caused inactive HER2 to accumulate at the cell surface, which strengthened trastuzumab-mediated killing of HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells.
The irreversible TKI pyrotinib drove HER2 internalization in gastric cancer models, raised cellular uptake of T-DXd, and improved tumor growth suppression in NCI-N87 xenografts.

developability: Both drug classes are already approved, so a priming-then-ADC schedule could in principle be tested without new chemistry. What is missing is any HER2-low or ovarian data and a worked-out sequence and timing, since reversible and irreversible TKIs push HER2 in opposite directions.
risks: Reversible and irreversible TKIs move HER2 in opposite ways, so the wrong agent or schedule could cut rather than raise ADC delivery
All data are in HER2-amplified models; the absolute lift in a 1+ tumor may be too small to register
Adding a TKI brings its own diarrhea and rash on top of the ADC
caveats: Whether any priming raises an IHC 1+ tumor into a responsive range is the open question the idea rests on.

intervention_label: High-avidity HER2-low-directed T-cell engager / CAR concept
mechanism: A T-cell-redirecting therapy, whether a CAR or a bispecific engager, points cytotoxic T cells at surface HER2 in a way that does not depend on a chemotherapy payload. To act on a HER2-low (IHC 1+) tumor it would have to fire at very sparse antigen, which means a high-avidity or high-sensitivity receptor rather than the affinity-tuned designs now in favor.
rationale: Cell therapy is the main HER2 modality with no representation on this case, so it is worth naming. But the field is moving the other way: low-affinity HER2 CARs are being built specifically to ignore HER2-low cells, because HER2-low is the level found on normal heart and gut epithelium. A receptor sensitive enough to hit this patient's IHC 1+ tumor would, by the same logic, risk attacking those normal tissues.
novelty: No HER2-low-selective CAR or T-cell engager exists, and the published cell-therapy work is engineered to spare HER2-low rather than target it, so this is an undeveloped target concept with no clinical-grade construct.

key_manuscripts.finding: Low-affinity HER2 CAR T cells controlled HER2-high tumors while leaving HER2-low tumors, used as a normal-tissue surrogate, untouched. That shows current designs deliberately avoid the HER2-low tier this patient sits in.

model_systems: HER2 transgenic syngeneic mouse tumor models
developability: There is no construct designed to engage HER2-low, and building one runs straight into the on-target off-tumor toxicity that the affinity-tuning work was created to avoid. This sits well behind the other ideas here: the safety problem would have to be solved before a molecule could even be made.
risks: On-target off-tumor toxicity against HER2-low normal epithelium (heart, GI) is the central barrier
The cell-therapy field is deliberately engineering away from HER2-low, so the high-sensitivity construct this would need does not exist
No ovarian or HER2-low efficacy data of any kind
caveats: Included mainly to document why cell therapy against a HER2-low tumor is hard, not because a path is visible.

intervention_label: Biparatopic HER2 ADC (MEDI4276 / zanidatamab zovodotin ZW49)
mechanism: Biparatopic HER2 ADCs bind two non-overlapping HER2 epitopes with one molecule, which clusters the receptor and drives stronger internalization and payload delivery than a single-epitope antibody. MEDI4276 carries a tubulysin payload; zanidatamab zovodotin (ZW49) carries an auristatin.
rationale: Evaluated as a route to push more payload into low-antigen tumors, but these molecules have moved into patients, so they fall outside this forward-looking scan.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage: MEDI4276 ran a first-in-human phase 1 and was discontinued for poor tolerability, and zanidatamab zovodotin (ZW49) is in phase 1, so biparatopic HER2 ADCs belong to the trial screener. The MEDI4276 molecule was also already logged as a preclinical-evidence audit row.

intervention_label: Next-generation HER2 ADCs with novel payloads/linkers (BB-1701, ARX788, A166, DHES0815A)
mechanism: A wave of newer HER2 ADCs swap in different payloads and linkers to widen the therapeutic window in lower-antigen tumors, including BB-1701 (an eribulin payload), ARX788 (a stable non-cleavable auristatin), A166 (a duostatin), and DHES0815A (a non-cleavable DNA-crosslinker).
rationale: Scanned as candidate next-generation ADCs that might reach HER2-low disease, but each has already entered human testing.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage: BB-1701, ARX788, A166, and DHES0815A have all run phase 1 trials, so next-generation HER2 ADCs with novel payloads belong to the trial screener rather than this preclinical scan.
